# Explain declarative DockLayouts adoption in real applications

Part of #18474. Blocked by #18476 and #18477.

## Context

This leaf turns the existing DockLayoutsAdoption guide into the practical stage-one integration guide for real applications. The host PR already updates its normative Decisions 1–2 in the same freeze as the API; this leaf delivers the broader explanatory rewrite and validated migration path.

The first-layout tutorial is a separate beginner deliverable. This guide answers how an application supplies ordinary panes, initial selection and existing document state without becoming a dock-engine implementer.

## The Problem

The existing guide teaches manual seed/mount and resolvePane as basic application responsibilities. Minimal normative corrections keep it truthful when the host lands, but do not by themselves explain integration: lazy modules, header/policy data, computed initial declarations, supplied-document precedence, runtime operations, and migration from the manual pattern.

## The Architectural Reality

- Target: learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayoutsAdoption.md; preserve its existing public route rather than adding a competing adoption guide.
- Its source registrations already exist in learn/tree.json and buildScripts/docs/seo/generate.mjs PRIORITIES. Change registration only if the actual navigation/title changes.
- #18476 is the source of truth for once-only consumption, current-document precedence, post-consumption assignment and declared-pane lifecycle.
- #18477 is the concrete manual-to-declarative example. Model detail remains in learn/agentos/DockZoneModel.md and public API JSDoc.
- Ordinary state/provider and component construction remain framework concerns; the guide must not invent a dock-specific provider registry or a reactive panes_ contract.

## The Fix

Rewrite the guide around a real application's integration decisions, validated by running the resulting code:

1. Declare ordinary panes with lazy module/ntype/className, header content, existing policy hints and normal component configuration. Explain pane key as a stable application reference, including two same-class panes with different configuration.
2. Declare initial zones, or compute the initial pane selection/placement at the exact lifecycle point supported by #18476. A static choice based on available application data is not a live authorization subscription.
3. Supply an existing valid dockModel when the application already owns one; demonstrate that its placement wins over defaults. Explain post-consumption assignment behavior exactly as shipped.
4. Use documented runtime operations and the host's standard declared-pane lifecycle after boot. Distinguish altering a future default from changing the current layout.
5. Migrate a manual graph/resolver consumer using #18477's before/after responsibilities. Name what disappears and what remains legitimate application work, including the example's existing perspective/tour code.

Keep detailed grammar and operation tables in the reference. Cross-link the first-layout tutorial when available, the existing runnable example, source/API reference and ADR. Teach no proposed perspectives, persistence, workspaces or reactive-bound-panes config.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Pane/configuration integration | #18476; Container/Card/Provider idioms | Ordinary lazy panes/header/policy and distinct same-class declarations integrate without custom engine hooks | Explain observed invalid/missing declaration behavior | Existing adoption guide rewrite | Run the worked application cases |
| Initial lifecycle and supplied state | Host's committed consumption contract | Computed initial selection is consumed once; supplied valid document wins; later assignment cannot reset current placement | State invalid-input and late-assignment behavior exactly as implemented | Lifecycle explanation and worked comparison | Supplied/default mismatch and post-move assignment controls |

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Source criteria 1, 2 and 4: a real application can supply ordinary panes, compute its initial selection at the documented lifecycle point, preserve supplied state and migrate from manual plumbing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Rewrite DockLayoutsAdoption.md into a complete real-application stage-one guide; preserve the same public route and the host PR's normative semantics.
- [ ] AC-2: Run the lazy-pane/header/policy example, two same-class panes with distinct configuration, and computed initial selection at the documented lifecycle point. Document observed behavior without claiming live rebinding.
- [ ] AC-3: Demonstrate supplied-document precedence against a deliberately different declared default. After a runtime move, a later panes/zones assignment behaves exactly as the host contract states and does not restore defaults.
- [ ] AC-4: Include a concrete manual-to-declarative migration based on #18477. The basic consumer needs no custom resolver/cache/projection hook; existing perspective/tour behavior remains application code until its own later stage.
- [ ] AC-5: Update the introductory `learn/guides/uibuildingblocks/DockLayouts.md` section "Adopting docking in your application" so it no longer teaches manual graph seeding, first-shell mounting and a custom resolver as the default adoption path; replace or redirect it to the shipped declarative guidance while keeping advanced raw-document support explicit. Cross-link the beginner tutorial, public example and detailed API/model reference without duplicating their catalogs. If the beginner tutorial is still pending, retain usable existing links and add its link in the later of the two guide PRs.
- [ ] AC-6: Render-verify the whole rewritten guide, including a useful diagram, snippets, navigation and links in the portal. The PR carries live-use grounding and exact-head evidence; prose-only review is insufficient.
- [ ] AC-7: Do not introduce later-stage APIs, API implementation changes, client-specific examples, tracker archaeology in learn/guides, or generated portal SEO output commits.

## Validation

Run the documented application/examples from the exact implementation checkout:

    npm run server-start -- --port <free-port> --no-open

Reproduce the guide's cases and open the complete guide through the portal navigation. Record the exact head, the compared default/supplied layouts, lazy/same-class observations and the later-assignment result. Verify source registration and link integrity with the canonical available guide/navigation checks; do not substitute a unit test for rendering or for executing the instructions.

## Dependencies and Decision Record

Native blocked-by dependencies: #18476 and #18477. This order avoids overwriting the host's same-PR normative Decisions 1–2 changes and provides a real completed migration example. The beginner guide may proceed in parallel after these dependencies.

Decision Record: REQUIRED at the parent capability; the normative ADR amendment is delivered by #18476.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with the host's ADR 0029 amendment. This guide explains the shipped API and does not reopen its design.

## Out of Scope

Beginner first-run tutorial authoring, exhaustive reference duplication, model/host changes, new example features, storage ownership, topology/window authoring, reactive catalog/authorization/history policy.

## Avoided Traps

No renamed copy of the old manual-resolver guide; no documentation of scratch functions as public APIs; no required import from projection/reconciliation/native-admission internals; no assumption that readable prose proves the code path works.
